children: Samsara delivered another quarter of 30% growth and raised its full-year outlook, pushing the stock more than 12% higher in after-hours trading on Thursday.
Samsara sells enterprise software and connected hardware to companies that run large physical operations-fleets, trucks, equipment, warehouses, field workers, and job sites.

The software company reported fiscal second-quarter revenue of $508.4 million, up 30% from a year ago and comfortably above the roughly $483 million analysts had expected. Adjusted earnings were 20 cents a share, compared with Wall Street estimates of about 16 cents.

Annual recurring revenue, a closely watched measure of the company's subscription business, reached $2.125 billion, also up 30%. Samsara said it added a record 242 customers generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue and 20 customers generating more than $1 million.

The company also boosted its full-year outlook. Samsara now expects revenue of $2.043 billion to $2.047 billion, up from its previous forecast of $2.005 billion to $2.013 billion. Adjusted earnings are expected to be 76 cents to 78 cents a share, versus its prior range of 70 cents to 72 cents.
Shares were up 5.3% in Thursday's regular trading, closing at $38.75. The stock has gained more than  9% year to date.
